issues.description: Email validation regex is too permissive and may allow invalid email formats. Does not comply with RFC 5322 standards and can be bypassed with malformed inputs.
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation library like validator.js or implement RFC 5322 compliant regex. Consider using /^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+\/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$/ or a dedicated validation library.

issues.description: XSS sanitization is incomplete and uses a denylist approach. Does not handle all XSS vectors (e.g., JavaScript URLs, event handlers, or encoded payloads). Vulnerable to bypass via encoded characters or alternative injection vectors.
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested sanitization library like DOMPurify or OWASP Java HTML Sanitizer. For server-side use, consider a library that provides context-aware encoding. Denylist approaches are inherently flawed; prefer allowlist validation.

issues.description: Email is not sanitized before being stored. While toLowerCase() is applied, there's no validation against email injection attacks or normalization of special characters that could cause issues in email systems.
issues.suggestion: Apply email-specific sanitization to remove or escape dangerous characters. Validate against a strict allowlist of characters. Consider using a dedicated email validation/sanitization library.

issues.description: ID generation uses Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure and Date.now() which is predictable. An attacker could potentially predict or brute-force user IDs, leading to enumeration attacks or IDOR vulnerabilities.
issues.suggestion: Use a cryptographically secure random generator like crypto.randomUUID() (Node.js 14.17+) or crypto.randomBytes(). Example: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; return `user_${randomUUID()}`;

issues.description: Input validation checks for falsy values but empty strings would pass the name validation after trimming is not performed. Names like '   ' (only spaces) would be accepted.
issues.suggestion: Add .trim() to input validation: if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim()). Also validate minimum length requirements for name field.

issues.description: Database query is commented out, making this function a no-op. This suggests incomplete implementation or placeholder code that should be resolved before production.
issues.suggestion: Either implement the actual database call or clearly mark this as a mock/stub for testing purposes. Consider using dependency injection to make database operations testable.

issues.description: Function lacks error handling for database failures. If saveUser throws an error, it will propagate but there's no transaction management or cleanup logic.
issues.suggestion: Wrap database operations in try-catch with appropriate error handling. Consider implementing idempotency checks and transaction rollback if needed. Log errors appropriately without exposing sensitive data.

issues.description: Name is sanitized for XSS but email is not. Inconsistent security treatment across user inputs could lead to confusion and missed vulnerabilities in future code changes.
issues.suggestion: Apply consistent sanitization strategy across all user inputs. Document which fields require which type of sanitization and why. Consider creating a unified input sanitization/validation utility.

issues.description: No input length validation. Unbounded input fields could lead to DoS via large payloads or database column overflow errors.
issues.suggestion: Add maximum length validation for email and name fields. Example: if (input.name.length > 255) throw new Error('Name too long'). Define and enforce reasonable limits based on database schema.

issues.description: Email regex is recreated on every function call. This is a minor performance issue when validating large batches of emails.
issues.suggestion: Move regex declaration outside the function as a module-level constant: const EMAIL_REGEX = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/; This allows regex compilation to happen once.

issues.description: No rate limiting or abuse prevention mechanisms documented or implemented. The createUser function could be called repeatedly to create spam accounts.
issues.suggestion: Implement rate limiting at the API layer (e.g., using express-rate-limit). Consider adding CAPTCHA for signup, email verification, or other anti-automation measures.

issues.description: No uniqueness check for email before insertion. Could lead to duplicate user accounts or race conditions if unique constraint is not enforced at database level.
issues.suggestion: Check if email exists before creating user: const existing = await getUserByEmail(input.email); if (existing) throw new Error('Email already registered'). Ensure database has UNIQUE constraint on email column.

codeQuality.summary: The code demonstrates good security awareness with parameterized queries, input validation, and XSS protection attempts. However, several medium-severity issues prevent it from being production-ready: (1) Non-cryptographic ID generation using Math.random() poses security risks for enumeration attacks, (2) XSS sanitization uses incomplete denylist approach that can be bypassed, (3) Email validation regex is too permissive and doesn't meet RFC standards. The code lacks comprehensive error handling, input length validation, and consistency in sanitization approaches. While the foundation is solid with parameterized SQL queries and basic validation, the security implementations need hardening with industry-standard libraries (crypto.randomUUID, DOMPurify, validator.js) rather than custom implementations. With these improvements, the code could easily reach 90+ score.

testCoverage.summary: The file fixtures/clean-code.ts has ZERO test coverage - no test files were found in the repository. This is a critical gap for a file containing security-sensitive validation and sanitization logic. The file contains 6 functions with multiple critical untested paths: (1) Email validation that determines data acceptance, (2) XSS sanitization that prevents script injection, (3) User creation with multiple validation branches, (4) ID generation requiring uniqueness guarantees, and (5) Database persistence with no error handling. Priority areas for immediate testing: all three validation error branches in createUser (missing email/name, invalid format), the complete happy path flow, email validation edge cases, and XSS sanitization with attack payloads. The async saveUser function lacks any error handling for database failures, which is a critical production risk. Estimated 18 distinct test cases needed to achieve adequate coverage of critical paths and edge cases. Given this is marked as an 'EVAL FIXTURE: Clean Code (Control)' expecting score >= 85, the absence of tests is paradoxical unless this is intentionally used as a fixture for testing a code analyzer itself rather than production code.

suggestions.description: Replace custom ID generation with the built-in crypto.randomUUID() method. The current implementation uses Date.now() and Math.random(), which could produce collisions under high load or in distributed systems. The standard crypto.randomUUID() generates RFC4122 version 4 UUIDs that are globally unique and cryptographically secure.
suggestions.benefits: Provides stronger uniqueness guarantees, eliminates potential race conditions in high-throughput scenarios, uses a standard format recognized across systems, reduces custom code maintenance, and leverages browser/Node.js native implementation which is more performant and battle-tested.

suggestions.description: Extract email normalization into a dedicated function. Currently, email lowercasing is inline, which makes it easy to forget or apply inconsistently across the codebase. A dedicated normalizeEmail function would centralize this logic and make it easier to enhance (e.g., adding trim, removing dots in Gmail addresses).
suggestions.benefits: Ensures consistent email normalization across the application, makes the transformation logic explicit and testable, allows easy enhancement of normalization rules in one place, and improves code readability by giving the operation a clear name that communicates intent.

suggestions.description: Extract validation logic into a dedicated function and introduce a custom ValidationError class. This separates validation concerns from the business logic of user creation, makes validation reusable, and provides structured error information that callers can handle programmatically (e.g., for form field highlighting).
suggestions.benefits: Improves testability by isolating validation logic, enables consistent error handling across endpoints, provides machine-readable error information for better UX, makes the createUser function more focused on its core responsibility, and allows easy extension of validation rules without modifying the main flow.

suggestions.description: Simplify sanitizeInput by using a lookup map with a single regex replace instead of four separate replace calls. This reduces redundancy, makes it easier to add or modify escape rules, and improves performance by traversing the string once instead of four times.
suggestions.benefits: More maintainable as all escape rules are defined in one place, better performance for large strings due to single traversal, easier to understand the complete set of escaped characters at a glance, and simpler to extend with additional character escapes.

suggestions.description: Add optional chaining and trim() to the validation check to handle edge cases where users submit whitespace-only strings. This prevents creating users with empty or whitespace-only names/emails, which would pass the current truthy check but are invalid.
suggestions.benefits: Prevents data quality issues from whitespace-only inputs, uses modern TypeScript optional chaining syntax, catches a common user input error pattern, and maintains backward compatibility while adding more robust validation.

suggestions.description: Extract the mapping between domain User model and database schema into a dedicated transformation function. This creates an explicit boundary between domain and persistence layers, making schema changes easier to manage and the mapping logic testable.
suggestions.benefits: Separates concerns between domain and persistence models, makes database schema changes easier to track and modify, provides a single point to handle field name conversions (camelCase to snake_case), improves testability of the mapping logic, and documents the database schema structure explicitly.

refactorings.summary: This is well-structured code with good separation of concerns. Minor improvements include modernizing ID generation with crypto.randomUUID(), extracting email normalization logic, and improving error handling patterns. Most suggestions are low-impact quality-of-life improvements rather than critical refactorings.

Replace custom XSS sanitization with battle-tested library like DOMPurify. Current denylist approach is incomplete and vulnerable to bypass via encoded characters or alternative injection vectors.
Add comprehensive unit tests for email validation function covering valid formats, invalid formats, edge cases, null/undefined inputs, and potential ReDoS scenarios.
Add unit tests for XSS sanitization with real attack payloads including nested tags, encoded characters, event handlers, and JavaScript URLs to verify security effectiveness.
Add integration tests for createUser function covering all validation branches (missing email, missing name, invalid email format) and error handling for database failures.
Implement RFC 5322 compliant email validation using a dedicated library like validator.js instead of simplistic regex pattern.
Add comprehensive error handling for database operations including try-catch blocks, transaction management, and proper error logging without exposing sensitive data.
Add tests for database persistence layer verifying parameterized queries are used correctly and error scenarios are handled gracefully.
Add tests for email normalization (lowercasing) and name sanitization integration within the createUser flow.
Extract validation logic into dedicated validateUserInput function with custom ValidationError class for better separation of concerns and structured error handling.
Add input length validation for email and name fields to prevent DoS via large payloads and database column overflow errors.
Implement email uniqueness check before user creation to prevent duplicate accounts and race conditions.
Add tests for ID generation uniqueness by generating multiple IDs in rapid succession and verifying no collisions occur.
Extract email normalization into dedicated normalizeEmail function for consistency and easier maintenance.
Simplify sanitizeInput function using lookup map with single regex replace for better performance and maintainability.
Add trim() to input validation to handle whitespace-only strings that would currently pass truthy checks.
Move email regex declaration outside function as module-level constant to avoid recreation on every call.
Apply consistent sanitization strategy across all user inputs (currently only name is sanitized, not email).
